newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq signs oil deals with foreign firms - minister.
newsitem.headline: Iraq signs oil deals with foreign firms - minister.

text.p: Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al- Sahaf was quoted as saying on Monday that Iraq had started striking deals with foreign firms for the sale of oil under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
"The oil ministry has begun signing contracts with international oil firms within the framework of the memorandum of understanding," Sahaf said in remarks published in Baghdad's state-run newspapers.
Iraq last month accepted U.N. terms for the partial flow of its crude oil to world markets after a six-year blockade under a U.N. embargo imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The deal signed in May provides for limited exports of $2 billion every six months to enable Baghdad buy food and medicine.
Sahaf said he expected the deal to be translated into action "in the coming few days."
He said a senior U.N oil overseer was due in Baghdad on Monday and will be joined by the rest of his group later in the week.

"The team of overseers consists of two action groups. The first comprising six experts will supervise Mina al-Bakr and the second comprising four other experts will inspect the gauging station in Zakho," Sahaf said.
Under the deal Iraq will have to pump the bulk of its exports via its pipeline through Turkey and the rest through its Mina al-Bakr port on the Gulf.
Sahaf said the U.N. would also send four more overseers to the Turkish port of Ceyhan to supervise the loading of Iraqi crude.
Four U.N. experts from Lloyd's Shipping Intelligence went to the northern Iraqi town of Zakho on Sunday to inspect Iraq's preparations for the flow of humanitarian goods under the oil deal.

The three experts under Ivor Lavers arrived in Baghdad on Wednesday. They are part of a forward team to examine Iraqi trade outlets prior to the implmentation of the oil for food deal whose conditions Iraq accepted on November 25.
